title: Leg Press
summary: The sled leg press: quads 1, glutes 0.6, adductors 0.5. Heavy leg training with little fatigue to the back and torso.

muscles.why: The quads straighten the knee; vasti 1, rectus femoris 0.4.
The glutes extend the hip from the bent position; more with the feet high.
The adductor magnus helps extend the hip, more with a wider stance.

setup.text: Back and hips flat on the pad.
Feet shoulder width in the middle of the platform.
Release the safeties before the first rep and keep a hand on them.

form_cues.cue: Lower until knees are deeply bent
form_cues.why: Lowering until the hips almost come off the pad uses the full range.

form_cues.cue: Keep your lower back on the pad
form_cues.why: Knees tracking with the toes keeps the hips sitting between the legs.

form_cues.cue: Press without locking the knees hard
form_cues.why: Stopping just short of lockout keeps tension on.

form_cues.cue: Keep the hips on the pad
form_cues.why: If they lift, you've gone deeper than your hips allow.

bias_tweaks.effect: More hip bend, more glute and adductor work.

bias_tweaks.change: Lower in 2-3 seconds and pause briefly in the stretch
bias_tweaks.effect: Keeps tension on in the lengthened position and removes bounce, so each rep starts honestly.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Rep speeds from 0.5 to 8 s gave similar growth; this is a control tool, not a growth trick.

mistakes.text: Letting the hips roll off the seat at the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Use the depth you can reach with the hips flat.
Use the full range; log the depth you use.

mistakes.text: Locking the knees hard at the top.

misconceptions.myth: Leg press doesn't build legs like squats.
misconceptions.reality: Free weights and machines gave similar growth.

misconceptions.myth: Every set has to go to failure to grow.
misconceptions.reality: Stopping a few reps short gave similar growth to failure in a meta-analysis; growth tends to rise as sets get closer to failure, but the exact curve is uncertain.

lower_risk.text: Ramp up before your first working set. For primary lifts the app suggests 50% x 8, 70% x 4 and 85% x 2 when the first working load is 60 kg or more, and 50% x 8 then 75% x 3 below that.
lower_risk.note: High-load warm-ups improved strength performance in a systematic review; the percentages are coaching convention.

lower_risk.text: Add load in small steps. The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range. Default steps for this equipment are 2.5 kg or 5 lb; your gym profile can replace them.
Aim for about 3 reps in reserve in the 6-10 rep range. Easy to push close to failure; keep the safeties within reach.
Set the safety stops, and keep the hips on the pad.
Pick a variation, range and setup you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Machine squat with a deep knee bend.
Barbell squat: more glutes and adductors.
One leg at a time with dumbbells.
Grew the rectus femoris where squats did not.

notes: Leg-press variations have not been compared for growth in a study the app cites.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
